simple.meaning: אִשׁ (ʼish) is a Hebrew object word meaning “entity , used only adverbially, there is or are.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.

simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H786. ish אִשׁ 2Sam 14:19 ; Micah 6:10 , softer form for the usual יֵשׁ (q. v.), there is, are. (compare Aramaic אִתַי , Arabic ; and on the softening of ye, yi to 'î , see Ew § 53 c Ol p. 425 Nö § 40 c .)
